claims.text: An adaptive, on-the-fly trained machine-learning potential can better capture the ab initio liquid configurations of multicomponent high-entropy alloys near melting than a conventional EAM reference.
Using the adaptive machine-learning potential as the thermodynamic-integration reference will enhance reference–target phase-space overlap.
Using the adaptive machine-learning potential will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD's traditional EAM references.
On-the-fly training with ab initio molecular-dynamics data enables the reference potential to sample a wide range of liquid atomic configurations.
The proposed method applies to high-entropy alloys containing 5–20 constituent elements.
The proposed method applies from approximately 0.9T_m to 1.1T_m.
The adaptive machine-learning potential captures many-body interactions and anharmonic effects in the liquid state.
Active learning and on-the-fly recalibration incorporate a diverse set of liquid configurations into the reference potential.
Training on diverse liquid configurations makes the reference potential more closely mimic the ab initio potential-energy surface.
Closer reproduction of the ab initio potential-energy surface broadens reference–target phase-space overlap and reduces thermodynamic-integration discrepancies.
The proposed method is expected to reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by roughly 50% relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
Conventional EAM references underrepresent the configurational complexity of the ab initio liquid state.
Underrepresentation of liquid configurational complexity by conventional EAM references leads to larger thermodynamic-integration uncertainties.
The method should be effective when augmented ab initio datasets reasonably sample the diversity of local atomic environments.
Performance may deteriorate when chemical complexity exceeds the training capacity or at temperatures far from the melting point.
Trends in elemental and binary liquid simulations using machine-learning potentials support the estimated 50% reduction in path mismatch.
The magnitude of improvement may vary with alloy composition and the scope of the training dataset.
